thought.text: The LDAP search test fails. Let me investigate the LDAP config mismatch.

reasoning_content:
The LDAP search test fails because the app is configured to use the LDAP server host `ldap` in web.config.php (`'host' => 'ldap'`), but the compose service is named `openldap`. Also the baseDn is `dc=planetexpress,dc=com` while the test users are under `dc=example,dc=org`. This is a pre-existing configuration mismatch in the repo (web.config.php uses planetexpress defaults). The reproduced test infrastructure may rely on defaults... Let me check the e2e test for LDAP search to understand what it expects.

Actually, the LDAP search form only appears when LDAP is configured and search works. Let me look at the test and the LDAP config usage. But this is a documentation-screenshot test; the core software installation is verified. Still, the guide describes LDAP test users as a feature. Let me investigate whether the app can reach the LDAP container.

web.config.php has ldap host 'ldap', port 10389, baseDn planetexpress. The ddev openldap container is at hostname `openldap`, port 389, baseDn dc=example,dc=org. Also `external_links: ddev-router:...` and VIRTUAL_HOST. There's no alias `ldap`. So LDAP isn't wired correctly by default — the web.config.php expects a `ldap` host and planetexpress data, but the provided ldap compose uses example.org.

Wait—but sample config local file (web.config.local.php.example) has a commented-out ldap block also using planetexpress. Hmm.

Maybe the intent is that developers override. But the test_users.ldif uses example.org. There's an inconsistency in the repo.

Let me check the e2e LDAP test to see what it expects.

Actually, let me reconsider task scope. The installation guide's core steps: ddev start, composer install, npm i, importDump, cp config. All done. LDAP setup section says test users load automatically. They do load into the LDAP container (verified user1 exists). The app's LDAP connection config mismatch is a separate application configuration issue, arguably beyond "installation".

But the LDAP search test failing suggests the LDAP integration isn't functional end-to-end. However, that test is part of documentation generation, not strictly installation. Still, I should try to make it work if it's a simple config fix, since the guide emphasizes LDAP. But modifying app config to point to openldap and example.org would be a reasonable post-install configuration. Let's check how LdapUtility resolves and whether there's an env-based override.

Let me look at the app code and whether ddev provides a hostname `ldap`.

Actually wait, the docker-compose.ldap.yaml `external_links` and network — the service is `openldap`. There might be an intended additional_hostname or the web config should use `openldap`. Let me check git history / other config. Let me grep the repo for 'openldap' and 'example.org'.

This is getting deep. The core installation is successful. The LDAP search screenshot test failing is due to the repo's default LDAP config pointing at a different server/baseDn than the provided compose. I could fix it to fully complete LDAP integration. Let me investigate quickly.
